newsitem.title: UK: Novartis rules out share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Novartis rules out share buyback.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals and life sciences group Novartis AG said on Tuesday that it did not expect to return value to shareholders via a share buy back "for the time being".

In an interview with Reuters, Novartis President Daniel Vasella said share buy backs had tax disadvantages in Switzerland, and there was unlikely to be a buy back "for the time being, until the tax laws change".
Vasella said the group had "strong" cash flow of 3 billion Swiss francs a year. "We hope that this will not just continue but improve," he said.

He added that the decision to increase the dividend payout ratio to 33 percent of group net income was the "major way" of returning value for 1996. He said this level "corresponds to about the medium of the international industry. Switzerland traditionally was rather low."

Vasella said: "current exchange rates, if they prevail, which nobody knows obviously, will have a positive impact of maybe 10 to 12 percent on the sales line. If you look at the profit line it comes with a little delay."
A recording of the interview will be broadcast on Reuters Financial Television's Inside Equities programme at 1145 GMT.
